Shard apiservers by resource type. # # api server cacher should have some locality property currently, we have a cache layer in api server, which is responsible for serving watch and list requests. but the cacher will cache for all kinds of resources. imo, since we have multi api server, the cacher should have locality property. le me explicate it with an example, i have 3 api servers, and i configure the nginx / haproxy as : - api server a is dedicated for all pod related requests by default, api server b and c are backups when a is unhealthy - api server b is dedicated for all node related requests, a and c are backups. - api server c is dedicated for other requests, a and b are backups. in such a case, it's fine that api server a just cache for pod, right? cache for all resources works though, it consumes much more memory and cpu, build more connections to etcd server. hence, i suggest the cacher works as follows : - only start caching ( list & watch form etcd ) when server the first list / watch request. if it never server any list / watch requests about a resource, it does not need cache for it. - have expiration policy. for example, if it has not server any list / watch requests about a resource for a long time ( this could be configurable ), stop caching for that resource and free the memory it used. just my thoughts for discussion. i could also work on it if it sounds good. @ kubernetes / sig - scalability

title: Fix bugs in daemonset controller and e2e tests
body:
This PR is a preparation to get daemonsets working on Mesos. On the way towards this, the following bugs were found and fixed by this PR:
- the e2e tests delete all node labels. Other e2e tests might rely on them, e.g. on kubernetes.io/hostname, or in the Mesos case on some other labels.
- the pods created by the daemonset controller don't have [INLINE_CODE] set, although the code suggests it should. Hence, they are scheduled by the scheduler first, hopefully onto the right nodes. During this time, the daemonset controller thinks again and again that the nodes have no daemon pod created yet. In the case of a slow scheduler you easily end up with tens of pods for a 2 node setup.
- the daemonset e2e test checks for resource version conflicts and tries to update again. But it does not base the update on the newest version. Hence, when the version conflict occurs, the code won't be able to fix it.

title: Adjust memory overcommit on node for QoS
body:
With the current QoS policy, kubernetes guarantees that memory allocations will not fail up until the memory [INLINE_CODE] specified by the user. But the nodes are usually set up to fail memory allocations based on [kernel heuristics](https://www.kernel.org/doc/Documentation/vm/overcommit-accounting), if there isn't enough memory available to satisfy the request. A _Best-Effort_ container can cause malloc to fail for a _Guaranteed_ container. 
To avoid this, we can change the memory overcommit policy to never fail and let the OOM killer handle real memory allocations.
Kubelet on startup will have to run [INLINE_CODE].

root process in a container, container itself would be still running. 4. without userspace oom handling support, even kernel kills container's root process, kubelet might restart one to maintain sys oom situation. 5. today all containers are at root level, instead of using cgroup _ parent based on qos. this means, the root cgroup is easily get oom - title: Enable /proc/sys/kernel/panic_on_oops on nodes so that they don't go AWOL
body:
#12809 refers

Currently our nodes don't panic on oops, which causes them to simply go AWOL.

$ cat /proc/sys/kernel/panic
10
$ cat /proc/sys/kernel/panic_on_oops 
0

On Monday, August 17, 2015 at 12:46:00 PM UTC-7, Eric Northup wrote:

> Although it won't catch _all_ guest kernel problems, two mechanisms
> get you most of the way there: 1) reboot on guest kernel panic, and
> oops=panic.
> 
> To test for the first, examine /proc/sys/kernel/panic and make sure
> it's not zero. Also, enabling "oops=panic" might be worth doing (if
> that's not enabled, then the guest kernel "oops" encountered in the
> bug will not trigger anything, while it might have left a usermode
> thread unable to make forward progress).
> 
> See /proc/sys/kernel/panic_on_oops to enable the second (background:
> https://www.kernel.org/pub/linux/kernel/people/akpm/patches/2.5/2.5.66/2.5.66-mm3/broken-out/panic-on-oops.patch
> )

Some e2e tests are slow by necessity and design. Others are slow through non-optimal implementation. We don't want these to slow down the completion of the faster e2e tests.

title: NegotiateVersion is not working properly
body:
NegotiateVersion has several problems:
1. NegotiateVersion does not check group/versions exposed at /apis and prints a warning message when using kubectl to create an experimental resource.
2. NegotiateVersion takes the client#Config.Version into consideration, but it's not clear what value should be put in client#Config.Version as we have multiple groups now. We plan to create a config for each group, and calls NegotiateVersion for each group.
#14592 fixes the problem but it needs to be broken into smaller pieces to receive proper review.

In #14893 we temporarily disable the warning message in NegotiateVersion. We need to revert that when we have a proper fix.

@lavalamp @krousey

similar_issues.text: temporarily disable warning message in NegotiateVersion. when running kubectl to create a resource in experimental / v1alpha1, kubectl warns " server does not support api version'experimental / v1alpha1 '. falling back to'v1'". this pr disables this warning message. this warning does not cause any real damage because we set the default version before creating a client, rather than using the negotiated version. a proper fix is in # 14592, but it needs to be split to smaller prs and may not get cherry - picked to 1. 1. @ nikhiljindal @ lavalamp

NegotiateVersion happens too often. whenever a client is requested from the client cache, it negotiates a version with the api server ( https : / / github. com / kubernetes / kubernetes / blob / master / pkg / kubectl / cmd / util / clientcache. go # l63 ). for longer latency connections, this adds noticeable delays to every [ inline _ code ] command to gather information that doesn't change very often. if we don't change our approach, this problem will be exacerbated by api groups and discovery. instead of requesting the information every call, we could cache the api - version information locally. based on that cache, the client could choose a preferred version and simply force the [ inline _ code ] to that particular version. if we update the api server to add additional headers to the 404 returned when an invalid version is specified, the client could unambiguously know that the api - version is no longer valid. at that point we could clear the cache, give a good error message, and re - populate it on next [ inline _ code ] command. i like the idea of a separate cache instead of re - using something like a kubeconfig file, because there's no real reason for user intervention. i'd like to allow our tooling to mutate the local cache at will and kubeconfig files aren't the right place to make those kinds of modifications. @ smarterclayton @ jlowdermilk @ liggitt @ kubernetes / kube - api @ kubernetes / kubectl

kubectl negotiates api version to use based on client,server supported versions. manually verified this fixes the behavior observed in # 9755. [ inline _ code ] covers existing behavior when there is no version skew. left a todo to refactor so this can be unit tested properly ( refactoring required was a bit too heavy to do as part of this change ). fixes # 9755. cc @ bgrant0607, @ smarterclayton, @ lavalamp

Return errors directly from negotiation. kubectl displays a special error if connection was refused. negotiateversion is hiding this error, preventing users from getting the friendly message. in general, we should not mutate generic errors that come from connectivity, only those that are the result of an inability to process an error.

Fix NegotiateVersion. Split from #14592. split from # 14952. * * only last two commits are relevant * *. other commits are in other prs. 1. commit " fix negotiateversion " : let the negotiateversion use the serverapiversions ( ) function that checks both / api and / apis. 2. commit " hardcoding the config for v1 restclient " : the " fix negotiateversion " commit exposes a problem in clientforversion ( version ), which uses the config with the negotiated version to initialize both the restclient and experimentalclient, so sometimes the code will try to create a v1 restclient out of a config for experimental / v1alpha1, of course that wil fail. as a temporary fix, this commit hardcodes the config before initialize the v1 restclient. @ lavalamp @ krousey
